rules.title: The 45-day holding period rule, counted day by day
rules.summary: Franking credits attach to a dividend only if the shares were held at risk for at least 45 clear days around the ex-dividend date. The acquisition day and the disposal day are both excluded from the count, so the earliest disposal that keeps the credits is acquisition plus 46 days.
rules.example_heading: A parcel bought on Monday 2 March 2026
rules.example_footnote: Certain preference shares carry a 90-day count instead of 45. Disposals are traced last-in-first-out per parcel (s 160APHI).
mechanics: Count starts the day after acquisition: the acquisition day itself is day 0 and does not count.
45 clear days at risk are required; the disposal day is also excluded, which places the earliest credit-safe disposal at acquisition + 46 calendar days.
Disposals are matched to parcels last-in-first-out (s 160APHI), so selling any shares in the company restarts the question for the most recently bought parcel first.
The small-shareholder exemption (s 160APHT) applies to individuals only; an SMSF cannot use it, at any dollar amount.

rules.title: Franking gross-up arithmetic at the 30% company rate
rules.summary: A fully franked dividend arrives with company tax of 30% already paid on the underlying profit. The recipient grosses the cash amount up by dividing by 0.70, includes the grossed-up figure in assessable income, and receives the difference back as a tax offset, refundable for a complying superannuation fund.

figures.label: Accumulation phase: fund tax at 15% of $10,000
Accumulation phase: offset remaining as refund
Retirement phase (0% on that income): offset refunded in full

rules.example_footnote: Partially franked dividends scale the credit by the franking percentage; the divisor mechanics are unchanged.
mechanics: Gross-up: cash dividend ÷ (1 − 0.30). At 30% company tax the credit equals 3/7 of the cash amount.
The grossed-up amount (cash + credit) is what enters the fund's assessable income.
The credit then applies as a tax offset against the fund's 15% rate; for a complying fund any excess is refundable.
Income supporting retirement-phase pensions is taxed at 0% (ECPI), so on that income the whole credit comes back, subject to the 45-day holding period rule qualifying the credit at all.

rules.title: Bring-forward bands are derived from two caps, FY 2026-27
rules.summary: The non-concessional bring-forward bands are not published numbers: each band ceiling is the general transfer balance cap minus two, one or zero annual caps. When either cap indexes, every band moves. These are the FY 2026-27 values after the 1 July 2026 indexation.
rules.statute: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) s 292-85 and ATO published caps, FY 2026-27

figures.label: Standard annual cap only, balance under $2.1m
At or above $2.1m: non-concessional cap for the year

rules.example_heading: FY 2026-27 bands, derived from the two caps
rules.example_footnote: Eligibility is tested on total super balance at the prior 30 June and on being under 75 at 1 July of the contribution year.
mechanics: Band ceiling formula: general transfer balance cap − k × annual non-concessional cap, where k is 2 for the three-year band and 1 for the two-year band.
The general transfer balance cap indexed $2.0m → $2.1m on 1 July 2026, so every band ceiling moved by $100,000 on the same day.
The measurement date is the 30 June before the contribution year, not the day of the contribution.
A balance at or above the general transfer balance cap makes the non-concessional cap for the year nil.

rules.title: Carry-forward concessional contributions and the $500,000 gate
rules.summary: Unused concessional cap from up to five prior financial years can be added to the current year's cap, but only if total super balance at the prior 30 June is strictly under $500,000. A balance of exactly $500,000 fails the gate.

figures.label: Unused cap carried from the prior five years
Same unused amounts at a $500,000 balance

rules.example_heading: A member under the gate with $30,000 of unused cap
rules.example_footnote: Unused amounts expire after five years, oldest first, and the gate is retested against the 30 June balance every year.
mechanics: The gate is on total super balance at the 30 June before the contribution year, and it is a strict less-than: $499,999.99 passes, $500,000.00 does not.
Unused cap accrues from FY 2018-19 onwards and expires five years after the year it arose.
The current-year cap ($32,500 in FY 2026-27, AWOTE-indexed) is used first; carried amounts apply oldest first.
The gate is retested each year; a balance that crosses $500,000 pauses access without erasing the carried amounts that are still inside their five-year window.

rules.title: Minimum pension drawdown percentages by age band
rules.summary: Every 1 July, a retirement-phase pension recalculates its minimum annual payment: the Schedule 7 percentage for the member's age on that day, applied to that day's pension balance, rounded to the nearest $10.
rules.example_heading: Age 76 at 1 July with an $850,000 pension balance
rules.example_footnote: Pensions commenced during the year pro-rate by days remaining; a pension commenced on or after 1 June has no minimum for that year.
mechanics: The inputs are both fixed on 1 July: the member's age on that day and the pension balance on that day.
The Schedule 7 percentage steps at ages 65, 75, 80, 85, 90 and 95.
The product is rounded to the nearest $10. These are the standard rates; the COVID-era 50% reduction ended 30 June 2023.
Paying less than the minimum risks the pension ceasing to be in retirement phase for the year, which is an ECPI question, not a rounding one.

rules.title: Division 296 splits realised earnings across two tiers by balance
rules.summary: Division 296 commenced 1 July 2026. It applies additional tax to realised earnings only (unrealised gains are not taxed under the final law), proportioned to how much of the total super balance sits between $3m and $10m (15%) and above $10m (a further 10%, 25% cumulative).
rules.statute: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) Division 296 (Act No. C2026A00008)
rules.example_heading: A $15m total super balance with $900,000 of realised earnings
rules.example_footnote: Both thresholds are indexed from commencement ($3m in $150k steps, $10m in $500k steps); these are the commencement-year values.
mechanics: Attribution is proportional: earnings × (slice of balance ÷ total balance) for each tier.
Tier 1 covers the balance between $3m and $10m at 15%; tier 2 covers the balance above $10m at 25% cumulative.
The base is realised earnings under ordinary tax principles; the 2023 unrealised-gains design was not enacted.
Assessment is per individual across all their super interests, not per fund.

rules.title: 45-day holding period rule
rules.summary: A franking integrity rule requiring shares to be held at risk for at least 45 days (90 for certain preference shares) around the ex-dividend date before the attached franking credits can be claimed. The day of acquisition and the day of disposal are excluded from the count. The small-shareholder exemption (s 160APHT) that lets individual taxpayers skip the rule does not apply to SMSFs. The boundary is the entity, not a dollar threshold.
rules.statute: Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 (Cth) s 160APHO; Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 (Cth) s 160APHT (small-shareholder exemption; individuals only)

rules.title: Franking credit
rules.summary: A credit attached to a dividend representing company tax already paid on the underlying profit. A qualifying recipient grosses up assessable income by the credit and receives a corresponding tax offset; for complying superannuation funds an excess offset can be refundable.

rules.title: LIFO disposal tracing
rules.summary: The ordering rule the franking holding-period provisions apply to disposals: the most recently acquired parcel is treated as sold first. This is distinct from the cost-base choices available for capital gains tax, and it determines which parcel's day count a sale interrupts.

rules.title: ECPI (exempt current pension income)
rules.summary: The share of a complying superannuation fund's income that is exempt because it supports retirement-phase pensions, worked out under the segregated or proportionate method. A fund's ECPI position interacts with how its franking offsets land in the annual return.

sources.label: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) ss 295-385, 295-390

rules.title: Trans-Tasman imputation
rules.summary: The arrangement under which some New Zealand companies attach Australian franking credits to their dividends. Those Australian credits are recognised for Australian shareholders; New Zealand imputation credits, by contrast, are not claimable in Australia and are informational only in an Australian return.

rules.title: Qualified person
rules.summary: The status a taxpayer needs in relation to a franked dividend for the franking credit and tax offset to be available. Where the qualified-person tests are not met, most commonly through the 45-day holding period rule, the gross-up and offset are denied for that distribution.

rules.title: Contribution caps and total super balance thresholds, FY 2024-25
rules.summary: For the financial year starting 1 July 2024: concessional cap $30,000, non-concessional cap $120,000 (four times the concessional cap), general transfer balance cap $1,900,000. The non-concessional cap is nil when total super balance at the prior 30 June is at or above the general transfer balance cap. Bring-forward bands are derived: three years available below $1,660,000, two years below $1,780,000. Carry-forward of unused concessional cap needs a prior 30 June balance strictly under $500,000.
rules.statute: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) ss 291-20, 292-85; ATO published caps

figures.label: Three-year bring-forward available while TSB below
Two-year bring-forward available while TSB below

mechanics: Non-concessional cap = 4 x concessional cap.
Bring-forward band k is available while prior 30 June TSB is below general TBC minus (k minus 1) x non-concessional cap, and the member is under 75 on 1 July.
Exceeding the annual non-concessional cap in a year triggers the bring-forward period.
Carry-forward: unused concessional cap from up to five prior years is available only while prior 30 June TSB is strictly under the gate.

rules.title: Division 296 thresholds and rates at commencement
rules.summary: Division 296 commenced 1 July 2026 and applies to realised earnings only. Tier 1 is 15% on the share of earnings attributable to total super balance between $3,000,000 and $10,000,000; tier 2 is 25% on the share above $10,000,000. Total super balance is first tested at 30 June 2027. Both thresholds are indexed from commencement.
rules.statute: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) Division 296 (Act No. C2026A00008)
mechanics: tier 1 tax = rate1 x earnings x (min(TSB, upper) minus lower) / TSB
tier 2 tax = rate2 x earnings x (TSB minus upper) / TSB
Assessed per individual across all super interests, not per fund.
